title: Luke's witness: the birth at Bethlehem

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 14, cols. A-B (PDF p. 38)

source_text: Non enim soli Ioseph, sed et Dei genitrici Mariae testimonium perhibens Lucas, in divinis Evangeliis, ad ipsam David familiam atque cognationem respiciens, enarrat ac dicit: Ascendit autem et Ioseph a Galilaea in civitatem Iudaeae, quae vocatur Bethleem, ut profiteretur cum Maria desponsata sibi uxore, praegnante: eo quod essent ipsi e domo et familia David. Factum est autem, cum essent ipsi ibi, impleti sunt dies ut pareret ipsa, et peperit filium suum primogenitum omnis creaturae: et pannis eum involuit, et reclinavit ipsum in praesepio, quia non erat eis locus in diversorio.
pass_a_gloss: For not to Joseph alone (soli), but also to Mary the God-bearer (Dei genitrix) giving testimony (testimonium perhibens) Luke, in the divine Gospels (divina Evangelia), looking back (respiciens) to the very family (familia) and kindred (cognatio) of David, narrates (enarrat) and says: And Joseph also went up (ascendit) from Galilee into a city of Judea, which is called Bethlehem, that he might be registered (profiteretur) with Mary his betrothed (desponsata) wife, pregnant (praegnante): because they were from the house and family of David. And it happened, when they were there, the days were filled (impleti sunt dies) that she should give birth (pareret), and she bore (peperit) her son the firstborn of all creation (primogenitum omnis creaturae): and wrapped (involuit) Him in cloths (panni), and laid (reclinavit) Him in a manger (praesepium), because there was not for them a place (locus) in the inn (diversorium).

choices.choice: 'primogenitum omnis creaturae' is the author's blend of Luke 2:7 ('firstborn son') with Colossians 1:15 ('firstborn of all creation'); rendered once as 'her son, the firstborn of all creation' and cited to Colossians 1:15 beside the clause.

choices.issue: because they were of the house ... of David
choices.choice: The print puts the Bethlehem clause before 'because they were of the house ... of David'; that order is kept.
Margin variant 'al. solum' at 'soli' not adopted.
'pannis' rendered 'cloths' to keep it distinct from 'fasciis' ('swaddling bands') in section 17.

pass_b_english: For Luke, bearing witness in the divine Gospels not to Joseph alone but also to Mary the Mother of God, and looking to the very family and kindred of David, tells the story and says: And Joseph also went up from Galilee to a city of Judea called Bethlehem, to be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was with child, because they were of the house and family of David (Luke 2:4-5). And it happened that while they were there, the days were fulfilled for her to give birth; and she brought forth her son, the firstborn of all creation (Colossians 1:15), and wrapped Him in cloths and laid Him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn (Luke 2:6-7).
notes: Margins 'Luc. 2', 'Ibidem': Luke 2:4-7. 'primogenitum omnis creaturae' is the author's blend of Luke 2:7 ('firstborn son') with Colossians 1:15 ('firstborn of all creation'); rendered once as 'her son, the firstborn of all creation' and cited to Colossians 1:15 beside the clause. The print puts the Bethlehem clause before 'because they were of the house ... of David'; that order is kept. 'Dei genitrix' rendered 'Mother of God' (Theotokos). Margin variant 'al. solum' at 'soli' not adopted. 'pannis' rendered 'cloths' to keep it distinct from 'fasciis' ('swaddling bands') in section 17.
source_notes: PDF p. 38 = printed p. 14, cols. A-B. Margins 'Luc. 2', 'Ibidem' (Luke 2:4-7). Margin at 'soli': 'al. solum'. 'primogenitum omnis creaturae' is the author's blend with Colossians 1:15. The order of clauses (Bethlehem clause before 'eo quod essent ... David') is as printed.
